plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Trees that look as if they are wrapped in lavender mist. Clusters of trumpet-shaped violet-blue flowers cover the branches and then drift down to make soft purple carpets on pavements, lawns and parked cars.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring in Australia, from about October to early December. Blooming peaks in northern areas first and arrives later in the south, so Melbourne's display falls around late November and early December.
plants.location: Sydney and Melbourne, southeastern Australia, where the South American native is widely planted as a street tree
plants.funFact: Jacarandas are so closely tied to exam season in parts of Australia that students have long joked that a flower landing on your head means you will pass. The tree actually comes from South America.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An elegant evergreen shrub that flowers when most of the garden is winding down. Its glossy dark leaves set off silky single or semi-double blooms with golden stamens, and many varieties are lightly fragrant.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn into early winter, generally from October through December or January, with peak bloom around mid-November in many gardens
plants.location: Gardens in the southeastern United States, such as Charleston, South Carolina, and other mild temperate regions. It is native to Japan.
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is related to the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. Its seeds are pressed for an edible and cosmetic oil in Japan and China.

plants.name: Schlumbergera truncata
plants.description: A jungle cactus with no spines. Its flat, scalloped, segmented stems arch downward, and each tip ends in an exotic flower in tiered, tubular layers. The blooms attract hummingbirds in the wild.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-November to late December, sometimes into January, which makes it a reliable holiday bloomer
plants.location: Native to the Atlantic Forest (Mata Atlântica) of southeastern Brazil, where it grows on trees and rocks. It is now popular as a houseplant around the world.
plants.funFact: It is an epiphyte, so in the wild it perches on tree branches and rocks and takes moisture from humid air. It also blooms in response to shorter days and cooler nights, which is why it flowers around the holidays indoors.
